title.narrative: Output 1.1. Increased institutional capacity of employer and business membership organizations (EBMOs)

description.narrative:
In March 2023, the Georgian Employers Association (GEA) launched a position paper addressing critical bottlenecks in the implementation of the new Georgian Labour Code. GEA conducted survey among 500 Georgian employers in Feb2022, identifying issues such as the recording of working hours, which poses a particular challenge for SMEs. Following the research analysis, GEA developed a position paper addressing these challenges, adopted by GEA’s board in March 2023. Simultaneously GEA embarked on an advocacy campaign to promote their position on this issue. This campaign included a meetings with employers, discussions on potential solutions, and a presentation to the Tripartite Social Dialogue Commission in Dec 2022. The culminating part of GEA’s advocacy campaign was a round table held in March 2023, where GEA presented its position to Government and Parliament representatives, the Georgian Trade Union Confederation, business community members, and the media. GEA organized a press conference as well, which garnered extensive media coverage of GEA’s position.
In April 2022, GEA adopted a policy paper on facilitating SME’s access to finance. This paper drew from secondary data research and consultations with enterprises through focus groups. This policy paper recognized the key challenges in access to finance for SMEs and proposed multi-stakeholder policy proposals to address them. Following the paper’s release, GEA held a conference in Oct 2022 to engage in a dialogue with key institutions in finance, including the Ministry of Finance, Central Bank, micro finance institutions and SME agencies to explore joint solutions. As a result, GEA, in partnership with these institutions, formed a working group to develop an action plan based on the policy paper’s recommendations. In Dec 2022, the working group convened to develop the action plan, which was adopted in Feb 2023. With the support of the Danish Government, the ILO assisted GEA in developing and conducting a survey aimed at 500 Georgian employers. The ILO worked with GEA’s policy and research staff to help build the survey questionnaire and identify target groups. This involvement allowed GEA staff to enhance their skills in creating analytical questionnaires. Subsequently, the ILO provided guidance to GEA in organizing three focus group discussions with employers. These discussions served to corroborate the survey data and analyse its findings. By their involvement in the focus group discussions, GEA secretariat also increased their abilities in presenting the analytical findings, discussing possible solutions, and formulated proposals. The ILO support to GEA extended to data analysis from the survey and focus groups, the formulation of legislative proposals which based on research findings, and ensuring alignment of the proposals with international treaties, including ILS, to which Georgia is a signatory. The ILO arranged for relevant experts to participate in a high visibility event for the launch of the position paper. Specifically, the ILO supported GEA to demonstrate its capacity to draw on the knowledge of others, present and defend their position, and establish themselves as a credible partner capable of addressing complex issues. Finally, the ILO supported GEA to develop an advocacy campaign, allowing for targeted actions to raise awareness, influence policymakers and mobilize media support for envisioned changes.
With RBSA, the ILO supported GEA to develop a policy paper on access to finance for SMEs, and to organize a conference with key stakeholders on ways to improve access to finance for SMEs. In particular, the ILO trained GEA staff on aspects to consider when developing a position on SMEs’ access to finance by providing examples of positions developed by other EBMOs and offering a policy template that could be tailored to the Georgian context.
